name: Pop-overs
author: Fannie Merritt Farmer (1896)
steps: Mix salt and flour; add milk gradually, in order to obtain a smooth batter.
Add egg, beaten until light, and butter; beat two minutes,—using Dover egg-beater,—turn into hissing hot buttered iron gem pans, and bake thirty to thirty-five minutes in a hot oven.
They may be baked in buttered earthen cups, when the bottom will have a glazed appearance.
Small round iron gem pans are best for Pop-overs.

culture.text: From The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896) by Fannie Merritt Farmer. It popularized level, standardized measurements (cups and spoons) in American home kitchens, and stayed one of the best-selling cookbooks in the United States for decades.
